proceso.title: How I work
proceso.intro: An end-to-end method: from the problem to the data that confirms the goal was met. Six stages that feed one another.

steps.title: Discovery

steps.title: UX

steps.title: Prototyping

meta.description: What cookies and technologies franciscolopez.es uses, why, and how to manage or withdraw your consent.

cookies.title: Cookie policy
cookies.lead: This site uses the minimum of cookies and similar technologies. Here's what they are, what they're for, and how to control them. No analytics cookie loads without your consent.
cookies.whatBody: Cookies are small files a site stores in your browser. Equivalent technologies are also used, such as the browser's local storage (localStorage). Some are essential for the site to work; others, like analytics, are only used if you allow them.
cookies.useIntro: Here's the detail of what may load, grouped by category:

rows.name: flm-consent
rows.purpose: Stores your cookie choice so you're not asked again.

rows.name: Container (GTM)
rows.purpose: Manages the loading of the other tags. Stores no data on its own.

rows.name: _ga
rows.purpose: Distinguishes users in aggregate to measure site usage.

cookies.tableNote: “flm-consent” is kept in the browser's local storage (localStorage); it's technically not a cookie, but it's listed here for transparency. No marketing or advertising cookies are used today.
cookies.legalBody: Necessary cookies load so the site can work and need no consent. Analytics cookies only load with your prior consent, which you can give, deny or withdraw at any time without affecting how the site works.
cookies.manageHeading: How to manage or withdraw your consent
cookies.manageBody: The first time you visit, a notice lets you accept, reject or choose by category. You can change your choice —including analytics— at any time from the button below:
cookies.manageBrowser: You can also block or delete cookies from your browser settings.
cookies.thirdBody: Analytics is provided by Google (Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics), which processes data under its own policies. You can read them at
cookies.retentionBody: Your consent choice is stored in your browser until you change it or clear the site data. Aggregate analytics data is retained by Google according to the property settings (by default, a maximum of 14 months at user level).
cookies.changesBody: I'll update this page whenever the tools the site uses change. The date at the top reflects the latest revision.
cookies.contactBody: If you have any questions about this policy or want to exercise your data protection rights, email me at

meta.title: Brand Kit — Francisco López
meta.description: Francisco López's identity system: logo and geometry, the two-layer palette, typography and the rules that govern its use. Downloadable in light and dark.

hero.title: Brand Kit
hero.lead: Francisco López's identity system: the logo and its exact geometry, the palette with its two layers, the typography and the rules that govern its use. All downloadable, in light and dark.

concepto.title: A two-layer brand
concepto.lead: The symbol is a ring over a base: a lens, an eyelet, a zero. The split version offsets two color layers —cyan and purple— behind the ink stroke. It's not decoration: it's the signature of the method. From discovery to data, two planes that separate and realign into a single clean shape.

plano.title: Flat
plano.desc: A single ink layer. For small UI, favicon and monochrome.

split.title: Split
split.desc: Three stacked strokes, no blend. Only at ≥48px, where color reads as a layer.

logotipo.title: The logo and its rules
logotipo.lead: Two compositions —symbol alone and lockup with wordmark— each in flat and split. Cropped exactly to the ink: the height you give it is the real height of the symbol.

symSplit.name: Symbol · Split
symSplit.meta: Inline in markup · 382 B · sized by height.

symPlano.name: Symbol · Flat
symPlano.meta: Inline in markup · 220 B · sized by height.

symMono.name: Symbol · Mono
symMono.meta: One pure ink · 220 B · sized by height.

lockSplit.name: Lockup · Split
lockSplit.meta: Never inline · 23 KB outlined · sized by width.

lockPlano.name: Lockup · Flat
lockPlano.meta: Never inline · 23 KB outlined · sized by width.

usage.title: Usage table
usage.sub: All sizes are the visible height of the symbol.

items.title: Split → flat threshold: 48px
items.body: The color offset is 5.1% of the symbol height, so at 48px the crescent measures 2.5px. Below that it reads as dirty fringing, not as a layer.

items.title: Minimum size: 24px
items.body: The stroke is 8.6% of the height: at 24px that's 2.1px and holds; at 15px it's 1.3px and antialiasing washes it to gray.

items.title: No circular container
items.body: The symbol is already a circle. Putting it inside another shrinks it and turns it into a target.

items.title: Never smaller than adjacent UI
items.body: It's the brand, not just another icon. It must weigh at least as much as the LinkedIn or © next to it.

items.title: Symbol/wordmark proportion
items.body: 40–45% composed in UI, ~60% in a closed lockup. Outside that range the symbol floats alone or the wordmark dominates.

items.title: Nav transition: continuous
items.body: Color extinguishes before dropping below 48px and the wordmark fades in opacity without clipping glyphs. It never passes through a mis-registration state.

items.title: prefers-reduced-motion: jump
items.body: No interpolation: it jumps between states at once, with no intermediate transition. The symbol goes from 48px to 28px and the bar from 80px to 64px — two distinct measures.

ladder.title: Where the split stops working
ladder.lead: The color crescent is 5.1% of the height. Below 48px it reads as dirty registration, not as a layer. The ladder shows it on its own.

color.title: Palette and two layers
color.lead: The two-layer rule: an ink layer (background + stroke) that switches with the theme, and a color layer (cyan + purple) that only appears in the split and doesn't change between light and dark. Each swatch carries its token, its hex and its measured contrast ratio. Switch the theme with the nav toggle to watch the ink layer flip.

items.name: Purple accent
items.ratio: On inverted bg · 3.96:1 light · 3.48:1 dark · AA-large

color.pastelNote: Pastels never as text color. They're backgrounds. If text goes over a pastel, always in foreground (ink) — never the other way around.

tipografia.title: Two typefaces, two jobs
tipografia.lead: What the typefaces are and why, as a brand asset. The scale, sizes and line heights live in the Design System.

bricolage.name: Bricolage Grotesque
bricolage.desc: A grotesque with character — humanist details and slight irregularities that give it personality without losing rigor. It's the voice of headlines and the wordmark: firm, contemporary, recognizable.

inter.name: Inter
inter.desc: Neutral, with very high on-screen legibility at any size. It does the quiet work: body, labels, data and UI. Let Bricolage carry the voice while it sustains the reading.

aplicaciones.title: The brand in its place
aplicaciones.lead: Where the logo lives and how each piece is downloaded. The symbol PNG is sized by height and the lockup PNG by width — it's not obvious, which is why it's stated here.

favicon.title: Favicon
favicon.desc: A dedicated asset, not a rescale. At 16px the stroke rises to 10 units for optical compensation. Flat, centered.

og.title: OG image · social
og.desc: The real card served to social: split logo, wordmark, title and kicker over the brand background. Fixed in light and dark — each page generates its own. The lockup below is the piece that builds it.
og.previewAlt: Brand Open Graph image: split logo, wordmark and title over a dark background

aplicaciones.pngNote: The PNG suffix names the ink, not the background. tintaOscura (dark ink) goes over light backgrounds; tintaClara (light ink) over dark ones. Available at 256 / 512 / 1024 px.

uso.title: The real mistakes of this system
uso.lead: Not a catalog of generic ✓ / ✗: the failures this brand actually had, the figure that caught them and how they were fixed. A record of judgment.

cases.title: The viewBox that lied
cases.desc: It was "0 0 120 120" but the ink filled only 58% of the height. Everyone who used the component undersized it without knowing.
cases.fix: viewBox cropped to the ink — the height you give IS the symbol's.

cases.title: The split used at 24px
cases.desc: At that height the offset read as a print registration error, not a signature.
cases.fix: split → flat threshold at 48px (rule 1). Below it, the flat variant.

cases.title: The favicon with no optical compensation
cases.desc: The 16px one was the 32px rescaled; at that size the stroke washed out to gray.
cases.fix: dedicated 16px asset with stroke-width 10 instead of 6.

cases.title: The logo weighing less than a foreign icon
cases.desc: In the footer the brand sat below a UI icon and at the same visual weight as the © next to it.
cases.fix: the logo is never smaller than adjacent icons (rule 4).

cases.title: The lockup at 29%
cases.desc: The symbol grew and the wordmark lagged behind. The logo wasn't big: it was alone.

cases.title: The circle inside the circle
cases.desc: The nav put the symbol inside a circular container, turning it into a target.
cases.fix: no circular container — the symbol is already a circle (rule 3).

cases.title: The four colors of this page
cases.desc: The page documenting color was the one that had it wrong: bone, dark and the two pastels.

uso.boundaryNote: Identity goes here: what the brand is and how it's used. The engineering rigor —grid, breakpoints, spacing scale, motion and the full accessibility measurement— lives in the Design System.

meta.title: Design System — Francisco López
meta.description: The skeleton shared by every page of the site: grid, layout tokens, vertical rhythm, type hierarchy, light/dark, motion and the full accessibility measurement.

hero.title: Design System
hero.lead: The skeleton shared by every page of the site: grid, layout tokens, vertical rhythm, type hierarchy and light/dark behavior. It doesn't define any section's content — it defines how everything inside breathes. It's the internal criterion the site is built and audited against.

rejilla.title: Page grid
rejilla.lead: A wide container for layout; a narrow reading measure for running text.
rejilla.hint: The band marks the 12 columns — use the «grid» button above to toggle it.

cards.title: Container
cards.body: Max 1360px, centered. Above xl the margins grow; the content never stretches.

cards.title: Margins (page-x)
cards.body: clamp(1.25rem, 5vw, 2.5rem) — 20px on mobile, up to 40px on desktop.

cards.title: Reading measure
cards.body: Running text never exceeds 42rem (~91 char.) even when the container is wide. The classic comfortable measure runs 45 to 75 characters, so 91 is above it — a conscious wide-container decision, not an oversight.

tokens.title: Layout tokens
tokens.lead: This page's own contribution. They don't exist anywhere else in the system and move to the repository when the site is built.

cards.title: Fixed, not editable in production
cards.body: --section-y and --measure have fixed values: clamp(4.5rem, 9vw, 9rem) and 42rem. There's no tuning panel anymore — the rhythm is the same across the whole site.

cards.title: Defined once
cards.body: They live in the site's :root alongside the color tokens; each page consumes them. Changing a value here changes it everywhere.

breakpoints.title: Breakpoints

rows.change: One column, everything stacked. aside above the content. Type at the clamp minimum.
Buttons and metadata in a row; still one content column.
The aside + content two-column grid appears. Margins grow.
Full 12-column grid; aside can go sticky; 3-card grids.
Container caps at 1360px, centered. Margins absorb the extra width.

breakpoints.note: They match the repo's Tailwind scale. This document also applies fluid type and spacing with clamp(): between breakpoints the size interpolates continuously, with no abrupt jumps.

ritmo.title: Vertical rhythm and spacing
ritmo.lead: A 4px base scale (Tailwind). The air between sections is the primary tool of hierarchy.
rhythm: Between blocks within a section: 24–32px. Optional hairline divider.
Every section opens with a 1px var(--border) divider full width.

tipografia.title: Type hierarchy
tipografia.lead: Bricolage Grotesque (600) for headlines · Inter for text and UI. Fluid sizes: mobile = clamp minimum, desktop = maximum.

rows.name: Body L
rows.sample: I research, prototype, build and measure.

rows.name: Body
rows.sample: Senior Product Manager with 10+ years in B2B and B2C SaaS.

claroscuro.title: Light and dark
claroscuro.lead: Same skeleton, same surface hierarchy: background → card → border. No heavy shadows — depth comes from hairlines and surface contrast. Light is warm paper; dark is deep blue.
rule: primary is the only action color. secondary / muted / accent stay neutral.
Links, in two rules: primary for content links; foreground / muted-foreground for navigation chrome (nav, breadcrumb, footer).
Brand tones decorate or sign the logo — with one exception: brand-purple-accent is a brand tone used as text over inverted backgrounds (AA-large, ≥3:1). Splits and pastels, never as text.
claroscuro.ruleFoot: Use the header toggle to see this same page in both modes.

movimiento.title: Motion
bullets: Reveal = fade + 12px rise, staggered ~60ms between children.
Restrained motion: it never competes with the content.
prefers-reduced-motion: transforms and auto-scroll are disabled. Content always appears, even if the JS fails.
movimiento.navTitle: Nav transition — shared across the whole site
navBullets: Symbol 48 → 28px and bar 80 → 64px, continuously with scroll.
The split's color layers extinguish before the symbol drops below 48px — it never passes through a mis-registration state.
The wordmark fades in opacity without clipping glyphs: the gap only collapses once it's invisible.
prefers-reduced-motion: a jump between states, no interpolation.
movimiento.navFoot: It's the transition you're seeing right now in this page's header.

accesibilidad.title: Accessibility
accesibilidad.lead: The list each page of the site closes with. AA as a non-negotiable floor; AAA whenever it's reached without visual cost.

contrastRows.label: brand-purple-accent
contrastRows.note: Large text only (≥3:1) over inverted bg

accesibilidad.contrastNote: With this change, every text pair in the system reaches AAA in light and dark — none is left at AA. The one intentional exception is brand-purple-accent, which passes only as large text (≥3:1) over inverted backgrounds, never as body.
checklist: Measured contrast, with a figure, in both themes. AA is the non-negotiable floor; AAA whenever it's reached without visual cost.
Visible focus: a 2px ring with var(--ring) and a 2px offset on every interactive element. Never outline:none without a replacement.
Touch targets of 44×44px minimum, including small controls like the breadcrumb or the theme toggle.
A single h1 per page and an h2–h4 hierarchy with no skips. Reading order is DOM order.
Breadcrumb on every internal page, with <nav aria-label>, an ordered list and aria-current="page" on the current level.
Nothing encoded by color alone: any state or category distinguished by color also carries text or shape.
Text alternatives: alt and labels where they inform, aria-hidden on the decorative.

boundaryHere.body: The internal criteria and the measurements. For whoever builds or audits the site.

boundaryNext.body: The public statement: the level the site meets and how to report a problem. For a visitor. It doesn't live here.
